newsitem.title: USA: Lufthansa sees mixed air-cargo fleet.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees mixed air-cargo fleet.

text.p: Lufthansa AG will continue to stock its fleet with used or converted 747 cargo jets, but it has no plans to buy new models because of prohibitive costs, a top executive said Thursday.

Wilhelm Althen, chairman of the executive board of the airline's Lufthansa Cargo AG unit, called on Boeing to make unspecified changes that would make the current 747-400 freighter less expensive to operate.

But he told journalists at a briefing that as long as Lufthansa could buy used or converted 747-200 freighters for $40 million each, there was "no chance" it would spend $150 million on a new 747-400 freighter.
Althen said the chief drawback to the 747 was its need to make costly refueling stops on trips between most Asian destinations and Europe.

In September the German company announced it would expand its freighter fleet with an order for up to 12 McDonnell Douglas Corp MD-11s, which carry a smaller payload but have a longer range than the 747-400.
"Of course, at the time, nobody knew this would be a Boeing airplane," Althen said, referring to Boeing's planned acquisition of its main U.S. rival. "That came as a surprise to us."
